problem_complexity.detailed_justification:
1 self-limited or minor problem: Health maintenance immunization (PCV20 given). 8 stable, chronic illness: History of CVA (secondary prevention not on aspirin), Hyperlipidemia (LDL previously >200; repeat planned), Hypothyroidism (prior mildly suppressed TSH; repeat planned), GERD (off meds, doing okay), Chronic opioid use / chronic pain regimen (fentanyl and oxycodone continued), Depression (on SSRI; plan to reduce/taper), Asthma (infrequent inhaler use; follow-up), Sleep apnea (continues CPAP, tolerating). 1 chronic illness with exacerbation, progression, or side effects of treatment: Fibromyalgia with increasing pain. 1 undiagnosed new problem with uncertain prognosis: Memory problems (attributed possibly to opioids; neurology evaluation planned).
Fibromyalgia with increasing pain: A&P: "Fibromyalgia. She reports increasing pain from this. Trial of duloxetine 20 mg twice daily consider tapering up if works okay." Worsening symptoms with active treatment escalation supports chronic illness with exacerbation.
History of CVA (secondary prevention not on aspirin): A&P: "Apparent history of a CVA... Not currently on aspirin. I would recommend she take 1 of those. Baby aspirin daily." CVA is chronic and is being managed for prevention; no acute neurologic change documented.
Hyperlipidemia (LDL previously >200; repeat planned): A&P: "Hyperlipidemia. Her last lipids showed LDL greater than 200–repeat in consider lipid-lowering agents." Chronic condition addressed with diagnostic monitoring; no explicit statement of worsening/progression today.
Hypothyroidism (prior mildly suppressed TSH; repeat planned): A&P: "Hypothyroidism. Last thyroid level showed mild suppression of her TSH–will repeat." Chronic condition addressed with monitoring; no explicit uncontrolled symptoms or medication change documented.
GERD (off meds, doing okay): A&P: "GERD–doing okay off medications as well." Chronic condition assessed as stable without escalation.
Chronic opioid use / chronic pain regimen (fentanyl and oxycodone continued): A&P: "Opioid use. No change in her fentanyl and oxycodone." Ongoing chronic therapy assessed/continued without change, consistent with stable chronic condition management.
Depression (on SSRI; plan to reduce/taper): A&P: "Depression–doing well... we will cut that down to 100 mg daily and consider tapering further..." Condition described as doing well; despite dose reduction, A&P does not document exacerbation/poor control.
Asthma (infrequent inhaler use; follow-up): A&P: "Asthma–very infrequent use of her inhaler...–follow-up." Chronic condition assessed as stable with routine follow-up.
Sleep apnea (continues CPAP, tolerating): A&P: "Sleep apnea–continues on CPAP and tolerating okay." Chronic condition managed with device and assessed as stable.
Memory problems (attributed possibly to opioids; neurology evaluation planned): A&P: "Memory problems. I did point out that her opioids may have an effect here. She is getting neurology evaluation in the future." Symptom problem without definitive diagnosis and planned specialty evaluation supports uncertain prognosis (even without immediate testing ordered today).
Health maintenance immunization (PCV20 given): A&P: "Health maintenance–PCV immunization today." Preventive care action; not a disease problem and does not increase problem complexity.

em.pc_critic_response: Audit finding: the prior Problem Complexity level of Moderate is supported, but the original justification was incomplete and somewhat imprecise. The highest-level addressed problem is fibromyalgia with documented worsening ("increasing pain") and treatment escalation (trial of duloxetine), meeting chronic illness with exacerbation (Moderate). Multiple other chronic conditions were also explicitly addressed in the A&P (CVA prevention, hyperlipidemia monitoring, hypothyroidism monitoring, GERD, opioid use, depression, asthma, OSA), which were under-specified in the earlier summary. Additionally, "memory problems" is an addressed symptom with planned neurology evaluation and no definitive diagnosis, reasonably classifiable as an undiagnosed problem with uncertain prognosis (Moderate), providing an independent basis for Moderate even if fibromyalgia were debated. No A&P problem meets High criteria (no threat to life/bodily function or severe exacerbation documented). Assumption: neurology evaluation represents active diagnostic evaluation planning; no immediate diagnostic orders documented for memory complaint.
em.dc_critic_response:
1) DISC: I searched the note for explicit statements of discussion with another qualified health care professional (e.g., “discussed with Dr X”). The note only states the patient was referred/scheduled for therapy and will have a future neurology evaluation; these are referrals/plans, not documented discussions, so DISC is not supported.
2) Intpr (radiology): I checked for any imaging (XR/CT/MRI/US) orders/results and any language of independent interpretation (“I reviewed/independently interpreted”). The only diagnostic result mentioned is an event monitor (not radiology) and there are no imaging findings discussed; therefore Intpr is not present.
3) iHx: I looked for history provided by someone other than the patient (e.g., spouse/parent reports). History is narrated as the patient reporting, with no separate historian identified and no indication the patient is unable to provide history; therefore iHx is not present.
4) Tests & Documents count: I counted only unique tests/documents ordered/reviewed, excluding medication orders and vaccines. Orders documented: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Lipid Profile, TSH 3rd generation, and (from structured data) CBC panel. No external notes reviewed and no test results reviewed/interpreted in this encounter beyond historical statements, so total T&D items = 4 orders. This meets Category 1 (>=3 items) for Moderate data complexity.
